stem: A sentinel event occurs at a Joint Commission-accredited hospital. Which statement is accurate?

options.A: The organization should identify the event, examine root causes and contributing factors, and make improvements to reduce recurrence risk even if it does not report the event to Joint Commission.
options.B: Every sentinel event must be reported to Joint Commission because external reporting is mandatory.
options.C: The organization should delay internal analysis until Joint Commission requests it.
options.D: If the event is not reported externally, no formal internal improvement action is expected.

rationale: Joint Commission states that reporting sentinel events to it remains voluntary, while accredited healthcare organizations are expected to identify sentinel events, examine root causes and contributing factors, and make improvements to mitigate recurrence risk. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Differentiate voluntary external reporting of sentinel events from required internal safety learning and improvement expectations.
source_version_date: Current FAQ includes May 2026 alignment updates; accessed 2026
source_locator: Reporting — 'Will reporting of Sentinel Events to Joint Commission remain voluntary?'; Alignment Transition — organizational expectations
source_claim_supported: Sentinel-event reporting to Joint Commission is voluntary, but accredited organizations are expected to identify events, examine root causes/contributing factors, and make improvements to mitigate recurrence risk.
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — quality improvement, incident/event review and patient safety systems
correction_summary: Rechecked the current 2026 Joint Commission FAQ, including the announced 2027 transition, and preserved the distinction between voluntary external reporting and internal analysis/improvement. Difficulty set to medium.
audit_findings: Current Joint Commission FAQ directly supports A and explicitly states reporting remains voluntary. B-D contradict current expectations. Independent second pass passed.
